media.title: Orangutan Jungle School
media.plot: Orphaned orangutans learn essential survival skills at a rehabilitation center in Borneo before being released back into the wild.

media.title: Born to Be Wild
media.plot: IMAX documentary following Dr. Birute Galdikas as she rescues and rehabilitates orphaned orangutans in Borneo.

media.title: Green
media.plot: A wordless film following a dying female orangutan displaced by deforestation for palm oil plantations.

media.title: The Last Orangutan Eden
media.plot: Explores the last strongholds of wild orangutans and the people fighting to save their disappearing rainforest home.

habitat.description: Orangutans are the world's largest arboreal mammals, spending most of their lives in the canopy of tropical and subtropical moist broadleaf forests. They require large, connected tracts of lowland and hill dipterocarp forest with abundant fruit trees. Each night they construct a fresh sleeping nest from branches and leaves high above the forest floor.

threats.name: Palm Oil Deforestation
threats.description: Industrial palm oil plantations have destroyed over 80% of orangutan habitat in the last 40 years, continuing at alarming rates.

threats.name: Illegal Pet Trade
threats.description: Infant orangutans are captured for the pet trade after their mothers are killed, with most dying before reaching buyers.

threats.name: Forest Fires
threats.description: Peatland fires set to clear land burn out of control, destroying vast areas of orangutan habitat and causing direct mortality.

threats.name: Fragmentation
threats.description: Roads, rivers, and plantations isolate populations, preventing gene flow and limiting access to food resources.

culturalSignificance.overview: The name 'orangutan' derives from the Malay words 'orang hutan,' meaning 'person of the forest.' Indigenous Dayak peoples have long regarded orangutans as forest people deserving respect. Their human-like intelligence and gentle demeanor have made them powerful ambassadors for rainforest conservation worldwide.
literature: Reflections of Eden by Birute Galdikas
The Malay Archipelago by Alfred Russel Wallace
Among the Great Apes by Paul Raffaele
mythology: Malay 'orang hutan' folklore of forest people
culturalSignificance.symbolism: Represents the intelligence of nature, the interconnectedness of all primates, and the devastating cost of consumerism on wild places.
